title: The pool reference, the transfer price element and its template version, the approval reference, the instruction element names, the acceptance and refusal codes and the 'per agreement' timer have no source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-031, its Story paragraph, AC1 to AC3, Data table); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.22.1, A2.22.2, A2.22.3.1, A2.22.3.2, A2.22.3.3); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T5.3, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (row R-DIS-59); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-AST-22)
section: APP s3, s4 steps 5 to 10, s5 X4 and X6, s8 BR8, s11, s12.5, s12.8, s13, s14, s15; CON s2, s7 AC2, AC3 and AC6, s11, s12.5, s12.8, s14
description: The step needs seven names and no source gives any of them. R-DIS-59's condition is 'transfer_price from the template version' but no source names the transfer-price field, its template version element or where the price is read; no source names the pool reference, the committee-approval reference, the instruction activity's input and output element names, the instruction acceptance and refusal codes, or a duration for the timer cell that reads 'per agreement'. The legacy Data table names no table of the service at all and sends the result to decision_log_entry, the FSD field catalog of A2.22.3.2 lists only ACE-sourced asset fields and no transfer field, the TSD S5 T3.1 gives asset_sale eleven columns with no pool, price-version, approval or instruction column, and the ownership rows give no transfer operation.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-59 condition cell 'transfer_price from the template version' and timer cell 'per agreement'. Legacy Data table rows: recovery_case, assignment, v_ace_npa_sale, decision_log_entry, rule_row, and no asset_sale or listing row. FSD S5 A2.22.3.2 field catalog names eight v_ace_* fields only. TSD S5 T3.1 asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 and listing DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 with no pool, price-version, approval or instruction field. TSD S5 T5.3 gives the module one published event and no consumed one. Context pack ownership rows: two tables, six REST operations, one event, one job, one workflow, with no transfer operation.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the business analyst of the Asset module and the rwb-partner owner
proposed: Carry the placeholder on every such value in both slices, hold the pool as the set of asset_sale rows of the case, the price version and the approval and instruction references as decision-record and workflow-history facts, and let the baseline review fix the element names, the codes and the timer duration.

title: No source names an operation of the transfer step and the legacy endpoints table names operations of other steps
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-031, Endpoints table and Permission checks); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2); _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows: six REST operations; connection matrix row S5 Asset); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.22.2 integration points and steps)
section: APP s1, s12.1; CON s1, s7 AC7, s12.1, s19
description: The transfer has no provided operation anywhere. The legacy Endpoints table names POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings, of which the first is rwb-valuation's under the Ownership Map ruling and the second is the pricing and listing story's of this service; the FSD A2.22.2 describes three steps that act on a screen and writes nothing to an endpoint; TSD S5 T-A.1 gives the module five endpoints, none of them a transfer; and the connection matrix gives S5 to S9 a Temporal row and no REST, so the instruction cannot be a POST of this service. Both slices therefore declare the two asset reads only and carry the instruction and the case move as consumed or answered.
evidence: Legacy Endpoints table: POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/valuations access 'Asset and disposal C' and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings access 'Asset and disposal C'. TSD S5 T-A.1 inventory API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 as assets, asset, valuations, listings and rounds. Context pack ownership rows list GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, GET /assets/{assetKey}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings, POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings, POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds. Connection matrix row S5 Asset: P7 T, S4 E, P8 T E, S9 T E, with no R cell to S9.
owner_role: Solution architect and the S5 rwb-asset service owner
proposed: Declare no provided operation for the transfer, carry the instruction on the partner activity of 12.5 and the case move on the rwb-case row of 12.2, and record the two legacy endpoint rows as other steps' operations in both slices.

title: Neither slice carries a requirement id and the module requirement rows name no transfer requirement
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E4-031, metadata table with no Requirement row); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the reqs list of both slices); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (requirements served); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T8)
section: APP s18; CON s18; the reqs key of both fragments
description: The traceability of the two stories needs one sourced requirement and no source gives one. The legacy metadata table carries Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision and no requirement row; the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty; the FSD requirement rows serve FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08 only; and TSD S5 T8 traces REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 against those two features with the story column reading 'Written one epic ahead'. Both stories therefore trace to FEAT-AST-22 and record the empty list rather than inventing an identifier.
evidence: Legacy metadata table of RWB-E4-031 lists seven rows and no Requirement. FSD S5 requirement table maps REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-005 to FEAT-AST-01 and REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 to FEAT-AST-08. TSD S5 T8 tabulates the same ten rows against FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08. Plan reqs lists of RWB-S5-E4031-APP and RWB-S5-E4031-CON are empty.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the business analyst of the Asset module
proposed: Trace both stories to FEAT-AST-22 with the objective, problem and metric of FSD S5 A2.22.1, keep the reqs list empty, and let step D1 add a requirement row to the next version of the module requirements.

title: The asset table is absent from the Ownership Map table list while Architecture v5 and the TSD attribute it to S5
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5: tables asset_sale and listing); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset definition DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042); Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 (slides 19 and 41, rwb-asset scope)
section: APP s2, s3, s11, s12.7; CON s3, s7 AC2 and AC7, s11, s12.7
description: The Ownership Map lists two tables for S5, asset_sale and listing, and the transfer step reads a third object, the asset row that carries holding_status, book_value and the case link. Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 give rwb-asset 'assets taken on, holding, floor price, listings, auction rounds' and TSD S5 T3.1 defines asset with DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 as the service's object, so the row is read as S5 on the same reading the take-on story records. The mismatch is recorded rather than resolved by this WP, and no other service is given the object.
evidence: Context pack ownership rows: Tables (2) asset_sale and listing. TSD S5 T3.1 defines asset with the fifteen field ids DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 and T3.3 relates asset to recovery_case and collateral. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-asset the asset scope including holding.
owner_role: Solution architect and the data steward
proposed: Keep asset as S5's object in both slices on the Architecture v5 and TSD S5 reading, and let step D1 correct the Ownership Map table row in its next version.

title: The FSD S5, the TSD S5 and the Epics 3 to 8 Specification the two slices read are in review with empty sign-off tables and the realigned stories have no approval
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (document control, sign-off); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (document control); Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: Metadata row Status of both stories; APP s3, s14; CON s3, s9
description: The sources are not approved. FSD S5 is at version 3 in review with an empty sign-off table, TSD S5 is at version 2 in review with an empty sign-off table, the Epics 3 to 8 Specification is at version 3 without approval, and the D-RCV-60 run has no human approval step. The missing approval is recorded as an assumption, both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1), and no behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature.
evidence: FSD S5 document control gives Status In review and the sign-off table has empty Name, Signature and Date cells. TSD S5 v2 document control gives Status In review and its sign-off table is empty. Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 carries a document control block with no approval. Template and Rules R8.1 requires a change-log row naming D-RCV-60 and the tool line.
owner_role: Solution architect and the business owner of the Asset module
proposed: Keep both stories at Draft (realignment v1) and let the verification loop collect the sign-offs before any status change.

title: No source publishes the operation names and element names of the consumed rows the baseline must fake
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T5.2, appendix T-A.1); _work/msr/context/S5.md (connection matrix row S5 Asset); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-59 systems column); Recovery Microservice Architecture v5 (slide 19, rwb-asset IN and OUT); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (sheet APIs)
description: The baseline has to declare and fake four consumed rows and no source publishes their surface. The case-move answer has no published operation anywhere, the approval answer is carried by a child workflow whose element names no document gives, the rwb-source-data data product that carries the asset and sale facts has no operation name, and the partner instruction element and its acceptance and refusal codes are named by no source. The FSD and TSD give the contract dependencies only as module names ('P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices') and the Epics 3 to 8 API sheet lists case, treatment, guarantee, litigation, asset, debt-sale, write-off, proceeds and partner operations with none of these four.
evidence: TSD S5 T5.2 names the modules and no operation. TSD S5 T-A.1 lists five S5 endpoints only. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-59 systems column: 'Partner Portal, Calculation Service'. Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-asset 'TMP Partner: issueInstruction' and 'Decision: child: approval' as names only. Epics 3 to 8 Specification sheet APIs contains no case-move, approval, source-data or instruction operation of these shapes.
area: Contract, S5 rwb-asset and its neighbours
owner_role: Solution architect with the owners of P1, P3, P7 and S9
proposed: Declare each row as consumed with its owner, its call type and its budget, carry the placeholder on the operation or element name, and derive each fake from the published owner document until the owner publishes the name.
